stem: Use this supplied client policy, not unprinted course code. Response R1 has three 20 ms chunks a1,a2,a3: a1 has played, a2/a3 are queued, and its conversation audio extent is 60 ms. On speech-start, cancel R1, clear its queued audio, mark its response ID canceled, and truncate its conversation audio extent to the amount already heard. Then receive late chunk a4 for R1; commit new user turn U2; create R2; receive its 20 ms chunks b1,b2; finally perform one playback step. Canceled-ID chunks are discarded, and each playback step plays one queued chunk. Which final state follows?
topic: Demonstration of AI in Humanoid Robot
assumptions: The sequence and cancellation, queue-clearing, response-ID filtering and audio-extent truncation policies are explicitly supplied; the lecture does not print this state machine.
No playback occurs between the stated events except the final single playback step; the earlier a1 was already heard.
All earlier conversation turns and U2 remain; only R1’s audio extent is truncated. This model does not assert exact transcript-to-audio alignment or a returned truncated text transcript.
Cancellation/truncation succeed in this bounded model. No live API, audio device or course program is executed.

solution.justification: Clear a2/a3, retain only the 20 ms already heard for R1, reject late a4 by canceled response ID, then queue b1/b2 and play b1. U2 remains in conversation state.

optionExplanations.o1: Incorrect. This retains and plays old queued audio despite the explicit queue-clearing transition. Cancellation of generation alone is not the whole supplied policy.
optionExplanations.o2: Correct. Clear a2/a3, retain only the 20 ms already heard for R1, reject late a4 by canceled response ID, then queue b1/b2 and play b1. U2 remains in conversation state.
optionExplanations.o3: Incorrect. This accepts the late R1 chunk despite the canceled-ID filter, causing a4 to play before R2 audio.
optionExplanations.o4: Incorrect. Playback and filtering are correct, but this keeps unplayed R1 audio in conversation state rather than applying the supplied truncation.

steps: Initially, heard=[a1], queue=[a2,a3], R1 audio extent=60 ms.
On speech-start, cancel and mark R1; clear its queue; truncate R1 to one heard chunk, 1×20=20 ms.
Discard late a4 because it belongs to canceled R1.
Retain committed user turn U2; create R2 and append b1,b2 to the now-empty playback queue.
The final playback step emits b1, leaving b2 queued; heard output is a1 then b1.
